MCCHEAM316.name: Writing Art's Histories
MCCHEAM316.contribution: Art historiography provides methodological comparison without musical objects.
MCCHEAM316.topics: This course examines the history of art history as an academic discipline, tracing how scholars have understood and interpreted art from the sixteenth century to the present. Topics include art and history, aesthetics, meaning and interpretation, authorship and identity, and the challenges of art history in a globalized world.

candidates.assessment: Historical and visual interpretation provide relevant methods. Native American Histories includes bounded analysis of contemporary music. Film and Text treats film music and sound. These contributions do not provide a sequence in musical structures, critical listening, score analysis, period histories or musicological inquiry.

candidates.concept: Music, society, politics and cultural institutions
candidates.assessment: Media and Race and Native American Histories address music in the study of identity and power. Sociology, qualitative methods and art institutions offer transferable study of reception and cultural organizations. The work does not build sustained study of musical cultures, scenes or music institutions.

candidates.concept: Music, screen media and digital culture
candidates.assessment: This is the closest response. Film and Text treats film music; Introduction to Film and Media analyzes sound in film form; Media Archaeology compares sound fidelity and includes recording exercises; The Documentary includes audio genres and production; Creative Communication Laboratory explores sonic poetry. Together these support audiovisual analysis and production, with insufficient specialist music study to sustain the pathway.

closestChallenge: A plausible media-led sequence would start with Introduction to Film and Media and literary interpretation, develop through Media Archaeology and television/platform studies, then deepen through Film and Text, Media and Race, The Documentary and Creative Communication Laboratory. It would have substantial audiovisual, recording and sonic practice. Adding Indigenous music context, art institutions, qualitative methods and period history broadens the plan but leaves music as one subject among several. It does not establish cumulative critical listening, musical analysis, music theory or music history. The society-led response has genuine adjacent institutional and reception methods but insufficient music-specific study. The historical and analytical response cannot provide the necessary sustained musical objects and disciplinary methods. No additional candidate can supply this missing foundation. These are contribution findings, independent of term availability; no programme was selected or scheduled.
